\label{GromConv_dfn1}
Let $(X,J)$ be an almost complex manifold with  Riemannian metric~$g$ and
$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ be a compact Riemann surface. 
A sequence $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j,u_i)$ of stable \hbox{$J$-holomorphic} maps 
\sf{converges} to a stable $J$-holomorphic map $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u_{\infty})$
if
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),ref=\arabic*,leftmargin=*]

\item $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ is obtained from~$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ by identifying 
a point on each of $\ell$~trees of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$, for some $\ell\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0}$,
with distinct points $z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\!\in\!\Sigma$,

\item\label{GC1energy_it} $E_g(u_{\infty})=\lim\limits_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)$,

\item there exist $h_i\!\in\!\textnormal{Aut}(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ with $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ such that 
$u_i\!\circ\!h_i$ converges to~$u_{\infty}$ uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact 
subsets of~$\Sigma\!-\!\{z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\}$,

\item\label{psi_it2} for each $z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\!\in\!\Sigma\!\subset\!\Sigma_{\infty}$
and all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large,
there exist a neighborhood $U_j\!\subset\!\Sigma$ of~$z_j^*$, 
an open subset $U_{j;i}\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$, and
a biholomorphic map $\psi_{j;i}\!:U_{j;i}\!\longrightarrow\!U_j$   such~that 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\ref{psi_it2}\alph*),leftmargin=*]

\item $U_i\!\subset\!U_{i+1}$ and 
$\mathbb{C}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}U_{j;i}$ for every $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$,

\item $u_i\!\circ\!h_i\!\circ\!\psi_{j;i}$ 
converges to~$u_{\infty}$ uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology 
on compact subsets of the complement of the nodes $\infty,w_{j;1}^*,\ldots,w_{j;k_j}^*$
in the sphere~$\mathbb{P}_j^1$ attached  at $z_j^*\!\in\!\Sigma$,

\item condition (\ref{psi_it2}) applies with
$\Sigma$, $(z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*)$, and $u_i\!\circ\!h_i$
replaced by~$\mathbb{P}^1$, $(w_{j;1}^*,\ldots,w_{j;k_j}^*)$, and
$u_i\!\circ\!h_i\!\circ\!\psi_{j;i}$, respectively,
for each $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$.

\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

If in addition $X$ is compact, then Theorem~\ref{GromConv_thm2} implies 
that this moduli space is also compact.
Combining this with the remarkable property of the previous paragraph,
the constructions of \cite{BF,LT0,LT,FO} endow $\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)$
with a \sf{virtual fundamental class}.
It depends only on~$\omega$, in a suitable sense, and not an almost complex structure~$J$
tamed by~$\omega$.
This class in turn gives rise to \sf{Gromov-Witten invariants} of~$(X,\omega)$:
$$\blr{\tau_{a_1}\!\alpha_1,\ldots,\tau_{a_k}\!\alpha_k}_{g,A}^X
\equiv \blr{\big(\psi_1^{a_1}\!\textnormal{ev}_1^*\alpha_1)\ldots\big(\psi_k^{a_k}\!\textnormal{ev}_k^*\alpha_k),
\big[\ov\mathfrak M_{g,k}(X,A;J)\big]^{\textnormal{vir}}}\in\mathbb Q$$
for all $a_i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0}$  and $\alpha_i\!\in\!H^*(X;\mathbb Q)$.

Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp}

in Chapter~4 of~\cite{MS12}.

\begin{prp}[Carleman Similarity Principle, {{\cite[Theorem~2.2]{FHS}}}]\label{FHS_prp}
Suppose $n\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, \hbox{$p,\epsilon\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$} with $p\!>\!2$, 
$J\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)$, $C\!\in\!L^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)$,
and $u\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\mathbb{C}^n)$ are such~that 
\BE{FHScond_e} u(0)=0, \qquad
J(z)^2=-\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}, ~~
u_s(z)+J(z)u_t(z)+C(z)u(z)=0 ~~\forall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation}
Then, there exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$, 
$\Phi\!\in\!L_1^p(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R)$, and 
a $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic map $\sigma\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ such~that 
\BE{FHSconc_e} \sigma(0)=0, \qquad
J(z)\Phi(z)=\Phi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n},~~u(z)=\Phi(z)\sigma(z)
~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\delta}\,.\end{equation}
\end{prp}

\label{FHS_eg}
Let $\mathfrak c\!:\mathbb{C}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}$ denote the usual conjugation.
Define
\begin{gather*}
\wh{J}(z_1,z_2)=\left(\!\!\begin{array}{cc} \mathfrak i& 0\\ -2\mathfrak i s_1\mathfrak c& \mathfrak i\end{array}\!\!\right)
=\left(\begin{array}{cc} 1& 0\\ s_1\mathfrak c& 1\end{array}\!\!\right)
\!\!J_{\mathbb{C}^2}\!\!
\left(\!\!\begin{array}{cc} 1& 0\\ s_1\mathfrak c& 1\end{array}\!\!\right)^{\!\!-1}\!:\mathbb{C}^2\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}^2
\quad\forall\,z_i\!=\!s_i\!+\!\mathfrak i t_i, \\
u\!:\mathbb{C}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}^2, \qquad u(s\!+\!\mathfrak i t)=\big(z,s^2).
\end{gather*}
Thus, $\wh{J}$ is an almost complex structure on~$\mathbb{C}^2$ and
$u$ is a $\wh{J}$-holomorphic map, i.e.~it satisfies the last condition
in~(\ref{FHScond_e}) with $J(z)\!=\!\wh{J}(u(z))$ and $C(z)\!=\!0$.
The functions
$$\sigma\!:\mathbb{C}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}^2, \quad\sigma(z)=(z,0), \qquad
\Phi\!:\mathbb{C}\longrightarrow\textnormal{GL}_4\mathbb R, \quad 
\Phi(s\!+\!\mathfrak i t)=
\left(\!\!\begin{array}{cc} 1& 0\\ s\mathfrak c\!+\!\frac{\mathfrak i st}{z}& 1\end{array}\!\!\right),$$
satisfy~(\ref{FHSconc_e}).

Suppose $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold, $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a Riemann surface,
and $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a  $J$-holomorphic map.
If $u$ is not constant on every connected component of~$\Sigma$, then the~subset 
$$u^{-1}\big(\{u(z)\!:\,z\!\in\!\Sigma,~\textnormal{d}_zu\!=\!0\}\big)\subset\Sigma$$
is discrete. If in addition $x\!\in\!X$, the subset $u^{-1}(x)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ 
is also discrete.

For each $\delta\!\in\![0,\epsilon]$, we define 
\begin{gather*}
A_{\delta}\in L^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)
\qquad\hbox{by}\quad
A_{\delta}(z)=\begin{cases}A(z),&\hbox{if}~z\!\in\!B_{\delta};\\
0,&\hbox{otherwise};\end{cases}\\
D_{\delta}: L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\longrightarrow L^p(S^2;(T^*S^2)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)
\qquad\hbox{by}\quad
D_{\delta}\Theta=\big(\Theta_s\!+\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\Theta_t\!+\!A_{\delta}\Theta\big)\textnormal{d}\bar{z}\,.
\end{gather*}
Since the cokernel of $D_0\!=\!2\bar\partial$ is isomorphic $H^1(S^2;\mathbb{C})\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n$,
$D_0$ is surjective and the homomorphism 
$$\ti{D}_0\!:L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\longrightarrow L^p(S^2;(T^*S^2)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)
\oplus \textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n,
\qquad \Theta\longrightarrow \big(D_0\Theta,\Theta(0)\big),$$
is an isomorphism. 
Since 
$$\big\|D_{\delta}\Theta-D_0\Theta\big\|_{L^p} \le \|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\|\Theta\|_{C^0}
\le C\|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\|\Theta\|_{L^p_1}
\qquad\forall~\Theta\in L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)$$
and $\|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as $\delta\!\longrightarrow\!0$, the homomorphism 
$$\ti{D}_{\delta}\!:L_1^p(S^2;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\longrightarrow 
L^p(S^2;(T^*S^2)^{0,1}\!\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}\!\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)\oplus \textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n,
\qquad \Theta\longrightarrow \big(D_{\delta}\Theta,\Theta(0)\big),$$
is also an isomorphism for $\delta\!>\!0$ sufficient small.
Let $\Theta_{\delta}\!=\!D_{\delta}^{-1}(0,\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n})$.
Since $D_{\delta}$ is an isomorphism,
$$\big\|\Theta_{\delta}\!-\!\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big\|_{C^0}
\le C \big\|\Theta_{\delta}\!-\!\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big\|_{L^p_1}
\le C'\big\|D_{\delta}(\Theta_{\delta}\!-\!\textnormal{Id}_{\mathbb{C}^n})\big\|_{L^p}
= C'\big\|A_{\delta}\big\|_{L^p}\,.$$
Since $\|A_{\delta}\|_{L^p}\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as $\delta\!\longrightarrow\!0$, 
$\Theta_{\delta}\!\in\!L_1^p(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_n\mathbb{C})$.
By (\ref{FHScond4_e}) and $D_{\delta}\Theta_{\delta}\!=\!0$, 
the function \hbox{$\sigma\!\equiv\!\Theta_{\delta}^{-1}u$} satisfies
$$\sigma(0)=0,\qquad \sigma_s\!+\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\sigma_t\!=\!0\quad\forall~z\in B_{\delta},$$ 
i.e.~$\sigma$ is $J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$-holomorphic, as required.

(1) Since $B_{\epsilon}$ is contractible, 
the complex vector bundles $u^*(T\mathbb{C}^n,J_{\mathbb{C}^n})$ and $u^*(T\mathbb{C}^n,J)$ over $B_{\epsilon}$
are isomorphic.
Thus, there exists
$$\Psi\in L_1^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R) \qquad\hbox{s.t.}\quad
J(z)\Psi(z)=\Psi(z)J_{\mathbb{C}^n}~~~\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.$$
Let $v\!=\!\Psi^{-1}u$. By the assumptions on $u$, $v\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\epsilon};\mathbb{C}^n)$ and
\begin{gather}\label{FHScond_e2} 
v(0)=0, \qquad
v_s(z)+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}v_t(z)+\ti{C}(z)v(z)=0 \quad\forall~z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t\!\in\!B_{\epsilon},\\
\hbox{where}\quad
\ti{C}=\Psi^{-1}\cdot\big(\Psi_s+J\Psi_t+C\Psi)
\in L^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n)\,.\notag
\end{gather}
Thus, we have reduced the problem to the case $J\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$.\\

\noindent
(2) Let $\ti{C}^{\pm}\!=\!\frac12(\ti{C}\mp J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\ti{C}J_{\mathbb{C}^n})$ be the $\mathbb{C}$-linear
and $\mathbb{C}$-antilinear parts of~$\ti{C}$, i.e.~$\ti{C}^{\pm}J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\!=\pm J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\ti{C}^{\pm}$.
With $\lr{\cdot,\cdot}$ denoting the Hermitian inner-product on~$\mathbb{C}^n$
which is $\mathbb{C}$-antilinear in the second input, define
$$D\in L^{\infty}(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n), \quad
D(z)w=\begin{cases}|v(z)|^{-2}\lr{v(z),w}v(z),&\hbox{if}~v(z)\!\neq\!0;\\
0,&\hbox{otherwise};
\end{cases} \quad
A=\ti{C}^+ +\ti{C}^-D\,.$$
Since $DJ_{\mathbb{C}^n}\!=\!-J_{\mathbb{C}^n}D$ and $Dv\!=\!v$, $A\in L^p(B_{\epsilon};\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{C}}\mathbb{C}^n)$ 
and $Av\!=\!\ti{C}v$.
Thus, by~(\ref{FHScond_e2}), 
$$v_s+J_{\mathbb{C}^n}v_t+Av=0\,.$$
The claim now follows from Lemma~\ref{FHS_lmm}.

$J$ is a smooth almost complex structure on~$\mathbb{C}^n$ with $J_0\!=\!J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$, 
and $u\!:B_{\epsilon}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with $u(0)\!=\!0$.

Since the subset of the points of~$\Sigma$ at which $u$ and $u'$ agree is closed to infinite order, 
it is enough to show that $u\!=\!u'$ on some neighborhood of~$z_0$.
By the continuity of~$u$, we can assume that $X\!=\!\mathbb{C}^n$, 
$\Sigma\!=\!B_1$, $z_0\!=\!0$, and $u(0),u'(0)\!=\!0$.
Let
$$w\!=\!u'\!-\!u:B_{\epsilon}\longrightarrow \mathbb{C}^n\,.$$
Since $J$ is $C^1$,
\BE{FHS2a_e3}J(x\!+\!y)=J(x)+\!\!\int_0^1\frac{\textnormal{d} J(x\!+\!ty)}{\textnormal{d} t}\textnormal{d} t
=J(x)+\sum_{i=1}^ny_i\!\!
\int_0^1\frac{\partial J}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{x+ty}\textnormal{d} t\,.\end{equation}
Since $u$ and $u'$ are $J$-holomorphic, (\ref{FHS2a_e3}) implies that 
\begin{gather*}
\partial_s w + J\big(u(z)\big)\partial_t w+C(z)w(z)=0, \qquad\hbox{where}\quad
C\in L^p\big(B_1;\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb R}\mathbb{C}^n\big),\\
C(z)y=\sum_{i=1}^ny_i
\bigg(\int_0^1\frac{\partial J}{\partial y_i}\bigg|_{v(z)+tw(z)}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\partial_tw|_z\,.
\end{gather*}
By Proposition~\ref{FHS_prp}, 
there thus exist $\delta\!\in\!(0,1)$, \hbox{$\Phi\!\in\!L^p_1(B_{\delta};\textnormal{GL}_{2n}\mathbb R)$},
and holomorphic map \hbox{$\wt{w}\!:B_{\delta}\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb{C}^n$} such~that 
$$w(z)=\Phi(z)\wt{w}(z) \qquad\forall~z\in B_{\delta}\,.$$
Since $w$ vanishes to infinite order at~$0$, it follows that
$\wt{w}(z)\!=\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!B_{\delta}$
(otherwise, $w$ would satisfy the conclusion of Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1})
and thus $w(z)\!=\!0$ for all $z\!\in\!B_{\delta}$.

$$u,u'\!\equiv\!(v,w)\!: (B_1,0)\longrightarrow (\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1},0),

and $u,u'$ are $J$-holomorphic with respect to some almost complex structure
$$J(x,y)=\left(\begin{array}{cc}J_{11}(x,y)& J_{12}(x,y)\\ 
J_{21}(x,y)& J_{22}(x,y)\end{array}\right)\!: \mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\longrightarrow\mathbb{C}\!\times\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\,,

By the continuity of~$u$, we can assume that $X\!=\!\mathbb{C}^n$, 
$J$ agrees with the standard complex structure~$J_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ at the origin,
$g$ agrees with the standard metric~$g_{\mathbb{C}^n}$ at the origin, 
$\Sigma\!=\!\ov{B_R}$ for some $R\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$,
and $u(0)\!=\!0$.
In particular, there exists $C\!\ge\!1$ such that 
\BE{FHScrl3_e0} \big|J_x-J_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big|\le C|x|,  \quad \big|g_x-g_{\mathbb{C}^n}\big|\le C|x|
\qquad\forall~x\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^n~\hbox{s.t.}~|x|\le1,\end{equation}
where $|\cdot|$ denotes the usual norm of~$x$ 
(i.e.~the distance to the origin with respect to~$g_{\mathbb{C}^n}$).\\

\noindent
Let $\ell\!\equiv\!\textnormal{ord}_0u$ and $\alpha\!\in\!\mathbb{C}^{n-1}\!-\!0$ be
as in Corollary~\ref{FHS_crl1}, where $0\!\in\!B_R$ is 
the origin in the domain of~$u$.
Thus, there exist $\epsilon\!\in\!(0,1)$ and $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that 
\BE{FHScrl3_e1} u(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(z^{\ell}\!+\!f(z)\big),~~
\big|f(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell+1} \qquad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation}
Let $z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$ as before.
By (\ref{FHScrl3_e1}), there exists $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ such~that
\BE{FHScrl3_e2} u_s(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(\ell z^{\ell-1}\!+\!f_s(z)\big),~~
u_s(z)=\alpha\cdot\big(\ell \mathfrak i z^{\ell-1}\!+\!f_t(z)\big),~~
\big|f_s(z)\big|,\big|f_t(z)\big|\le C|z|^{\ell} \quad\forall~z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}\,.\end{equation}
We can also assume that the three constants~$C$ in~(\ref{FHScrl3_e0}), (\ref{FHScrl3_e1}), 
and~(\ref{FHScrl3_e2}) are the same, $C\!\ge\!1$, 
$$C_{\alpha}\epsilon \equiv (C\!+\!C|\alpha|\!+\!C^2|\alpha|\big)\epsilon\le 1\,,$$
and $|u(z)|\!\le\!1$ for all $z\!\in\!B_{\epsilon}$.
By~(\ref{FHScrl3_e0})-(\ref{FHScrl3_e2}), 
\BE{FHScrl3_e5}\begin{split}
\bigg|\frac{|u(z)|_g}{|\alpha||z|^{\ell}}-1\bigg|,
\bigg|\frac{|u_s(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}}-1\bigg|,
\bigg|\frac{|u_t(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}}-1\bigg|
&\le C|z|+C|\alpha||z|^{\ell}+C^2|\alpha||z|^{\ell+1}\\
&\le C_{\alpha}|z|\quad\forall~z\in B_{\epsilon},
\end{split}\end{equation}
where $|\cdot|_g$ denotes the distance to the origin in~$\mathbb{C}^n$ with respect to
the metric~$g$ and the corresponding norm on~$T\mathbb{C}^n$.\\

\noindent
Given $r\!\in\!(0,1)$, let $\delta_r\!\in\!(0,\epsilon)$ be such that 
\BE{FHScrl3_e7}
C_{\alpha}\bigg(\frac{2\delta_r}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell}\le r\,.\end{equation}
For any $\delta\!\in\![0,\delta_r]$, (\ref{FHScrl3_e5}) and~(\ref{FHScrl3_e7}) give
\begin{alignat*}{2}  

|z|&\le \bigg(\frac{\delta}{(1\!+\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell} &\qquad&\Longrightarrow\qquad
u(z)\in B_{\delta}^g(0)\,,\\

u(z)&\in B_{\delta}^g(0) &\qquad&\Longrightarrow\qquad 
|z|\le \bigg(\frac{\delta}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell}\,,\\

|z|&\le \bigg(\frac{\delta}{(1\!-\!r)|\alpha|}\bigg)^{1/\ell} &\qquad&\Longrightarrow\qquad
1\!-\!r \le \frac{|u_s(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}},\frac{|u_t(z)|_g}{|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}}
\le 1\!+\!r.
\end{alignat*}  
Combining these, we obtain
\begin{equation*}\begin{split}
\int_{|z|\le\left(\frac{\delta}{(1+r)|\alpha|}\right)^{\!\!\frac1\ell}}
(1\!-\!r)^2\big(|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}\big)^2    
&\le \frac12\int_{u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(0))}\!\!\big(|u_s|_g^2\!+\!|u_t|_g^2\big)\\
&\le \int_{|z|\le\left(\frac{\delta}{(1-r)|\alpha|}\right)^{\!\!\frac1\ell}}
(1\!+\!r)^2\big(|\alpha|\ell|z|^{\ell-1}\big)^2  \,.
\end{split}\end{equation*}
Evaluating the outer integrals, we find that 
$$\bigg(\frac{1\!-\!r}{1\!+\!r}\bigg)^{\!2}\ell\pi\delta^2
\le E_g\big(u;u^{-1}(B_{\delta}^g(0))\big)
\le \bigg(\frac{1\!+\!r}{1\!-\!r}\bigg)^{\!2}\ell\pi\delta^2\,.$$
These inequalities hold for all $r\!\in\!(0,1)$ and $\delta\!\in\!(0,\delta_r)$;
the claim is obtained by sending $r\!\longrightarrow\!0$.

If $(X,J)$ is an almost complex manifold and $g$ is a Riemannian metric on~$X$ compatible with~$J$, 
there exists a continuous function $C_{g,J}\!:X\!\longrightarrow\!\mathbb R^+$
with the following property.
If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is a compact Riemann surface with boundary,
\hbox{$u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a $J$-holomorphic map, 
$x\!\in\!X$, and $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ are such that 
$u(\partial\Sigma)\!\cap\!B_{\delta}^g(x)\!=\!\emptyset$, then 
\BE{MonThm_e} E_g(u)\ge \big(\textnormal{ord}_xu\big)\frac{\pi\delta^2}{{(1\!+\!C_{g,J}(x)\delta)^4}}\,.\end{equation}
If $\omega(\cdot,\cdot)\equiv\!g(J\cdot,\cdot)$ is a symplectic form on~$X$, 
then the above fraction can be replaced by the product $\pi\delta^2\textnormal{e}^{-C_{g,J}(x)\delta^2}$.

For $\tau\!\in\!\mathbb R$ sufficiently close to~0, define
$$u_{\tau}\!:\Sigma\longrightarrow X, \qquad u_{\tau}(z)\!=\!\exp_{u(z)}(\tau\xi(z)).$$
Since $\xi|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!0$, $u_{\tau}|_{\partial\Sigma}\!=\!u|_{\partial\Sigma}$. 
Denote by $\wh\Sigma$ the closed oriented surface obtained by gluing two copies of~$\Sigma$
along the common boundary and reversing the orientation on the second copy.
Let
$$\wh{u}_{\tau}\!: \wh\Sigma\longrightarrow X$$
be the map restricting to~$u_{\tau}$ on the first copy of~$\Sigma$
and to~$u$ on the second.\\

\noindent
By~(\ref{Egexp_e}), 
$$E(\tau)\equiv E_{g_J}(u_{\tau})-\int_{\Sigma}u_{\tau}^*\omega_J-E_{g_J}(u)
=\int_{\wh\Sigma}\wh{u}_{\tau}^*\omega+
2\int_{\Sigma}g_J\big(\bar\partial u_{\tau}\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\bar\partial u_{\tau}\big)
\ge0\quad\forall\tau.$$
Since $\omega$ is closed and $\wh{u}_*$ represents the zero class in $H_2(X;{\mathbb Z})$,
the first integral on the right-hand side above vanishes.
Thus, the function \hbox{$\tau\!\longrightarrow\!E(\tau)$}
is minimized at $\tau\!=\!0$ (when it equals 0) and~so  
\BE{Ediff_e2}\begin{split}
0=E'(0)
&=\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\bigg(E_{g_J}(u_{\tau})
-\int_{\Sigma}u_{\tau}^*\omega_J\bigg)\bigg|_{\tau=0}\\
&=\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\bigg(
\frac12\int_{\Sigma}\!\!g_J(\textnormal{d} u_{\tau}\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} u_{\tau})
-\int_{\Sigma}u_{\tau}^*\omega_J\bigg)\bigg|_{\tau=0}\,;
\end{split}\end{equation}
the last equality above uses the definition of $E(u_{\tau})$ in~(\ref{Egfdfn_e}).\\

\noindent
Let $z\!=\!s\!+\!\mathfrak i t$ be a local coordinate on~$(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$.
Since $\nabla$ is torsion-free, 
$$\frac{D}{\textnormal{d}\tau}(u_{\tau})_s\Big|_{\tau=0}
\equiv\frac{D}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\frac{\textnormal{d} u_{\tau}}{\textnormal{d} s}\bigg|_{\tau=0}
=\frac{D}{\textnormal{d} s}\frac{\textnormal{d} u_{\tau}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}\bigg|_{\tau=0}
=\frac{D}{\textnormal{d} s}\xi\equiv\nabla_s\xi, \qquad
\frac{D}{\textnormal{d}\tau}(u_{\tau})_t\Big|_{\tau=0}=\nabla_t\xi\,.$$
Since $\nabla$ is also $g$-compatible, 
\begin{gather*}\begin{split}
\frac12\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}g_J(\textnormal{d} u_{\tau}\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\textnormal{d} u_{\tau})
\bigg|_{\tau=0}
&=\bigg(g_J\bigg(u_s,\frac{D}{\textnormal{d}\tau}(u_{\tau})_s\Big|_{\tau=0}\bigg)
+g_J\bigg(u_t,\frac{D}{\textnormal{d}\tau}(u_{\tau})_t\Big|_{\tau=0}\bigg)\!\bigg)
\textnormal{d} s\!\wedge\!\textnormal{d} t\\
&=g_J(u_s,\nabla_s\xi)+g_J(u_t,\nabla_t\xi)
=g_J\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\otimes_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi\big)\,,
\end{split}\\
\begin{split}
\frac{\textnormal{d}}{\textnormal{d}\tau}u_{\tau}^*\omega_J\bigg|_{\tau=0}
&=\bigg(\!\!\big\{\nabla_{\xi}\omega_J\big\}(u_s,u_t)+
\omega_J\bigg(\frac{D}{\textnormal{d}\tau}(u_{\tau})_s\Big|_{\tau=0},u_t\!\!\bigg)
+\omega_J\bigg(\!\!u_s,\frac{D}{\textnormal{d}\tau}(u_{\tau})_t\Big|_{\tau=0}\bigg)\!\bigg)
\textnormal{d} s\!\wedge\!\textnormal{d} t\\
&=u^*\{\nabla_{\xi}\omega_J\}\!+\!\omega_J\big(\textnormal{d} u\!\wedge_{\mathfrak j}\!\nabla\xi\big)\,.
\end{split}\end{gather*}

compatible with~$J$,  there exists a continuous function

the function $\phi(z)\!\equiv\!\frac12|\textnormal{d}_zu|^2_g$ satisfies
$\Delta\phi\ge-A_{J,g}(x,r)\phi^2$.

Let $\gamma_r$, $\delta$, $C$, and $E(r)$
be as in the statement and proof of Lemma~\ref{JHolomreg_lmm}.
Thus,
\begin{equation*}\begin{split}
E(r)\equiv\frac12\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\!\int_0^r\!\!\!
\big|\textnormal{d}_{\rho\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g^2 \rho\textnormal{d}\rho\textnormal{d}\theta
&\le C\ell_g(\gamma_r)^2= \frac12 Cr^2
\bigg(\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\big|\textnormal{d}_{r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g\textnormal{d}\theta\!\!\bigg)^{\!\!2}\\
&\le C\pi r^2\!\!\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\!\big|\textnormal{d}_{r\textnormal{e}^{\mathfrak i\theta}}u\big|_g^2\textnormal{d}\theta
=2C\pi r E'(r) \qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).
\end{split}\end{equation*}
This implies that 
$$\big(r^{-1/2C\pi}E(r)\big)'\ge0, ~~ 
E(r)\le \delta^{-1/2C\pi}E(\delta)\cdot r^{1/2C\pi}\equiv C'r^{2\mu}
\qquad\forall\,r\!\in\!(0,\delta).$$
Combining this with (\ref{JHolomreg1_e6}), we obtain~(\ref{JHolomreg2_e})
with $\delta$ replaced by~$\delta/2$.

In particular, u|_B_R/2in L^p_1big(B_R/2;Xbig), barpartial_Ju|_B_R/2=0in L^pbig(B_R/2;Xbig). By elliptic regularity, this implies that u is smooth; see . nodes.raw_latex:
With $\mu$ as in Corollary~\ref{JHolomreg_crl}, let $p\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be such that 
$p\!>\!2$ and $(1\!-\!\mu)p\!<\!2$.
In particular, 
$$u|_{B_{R/2}}\in L^p_1\big(B_{R/2};X\big), \qquad
\bar\partial_Ju|_{B_{R/2}}=0\in L^p\big(B_{R/2};X\big).$$
By elliptic regularity, this implies that $u$ is smooth; see 
\cite[Theorem~B.4.1]{MS12}.
By the continuity of $\bar\partial_Ju$, $u$ is then $J$-holomorphic on all of~$B_R$.

\BE{CylEnerPf_e3}
\int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2
\le 4C^2\delta^2\int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2
+2\int_{\{t\}\times S^1}f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta
-2\int_{\{-t\}\times S^1}f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\,.\end{equation}
Let $\ti{f}\!=\!f\!-\!\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\!f\textnormal{d}\theta$.
By H\"older's inequality and Lemma~\ref{poin_lmm}, 
\BE{CylEnerPf_e5}\begin{split}
\bigg|\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!f\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg|
&=\bigg|\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!\ti{f}\!\cdot\!g_{\theta}\,\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg|
\le \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|\ti{f}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12}
\bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|g_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12}\\
&\le \bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|\ti{f}_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12}
\bigg(\int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|g_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta \bigg)^{\!\frac12}
\le \frac12 \int_{\{\pm t\}\times S^1}\!|u_{\theta}|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\,.
\end{split}\end{equation}
Since 
$$3|u_{\theta}|^2=2|u_{\theta}|^2+\big|u_t-2\bar\partial u\big|^2
\le 2|\textnormal{d} u|^2 + 8\big|\bar\partial u\big|^2\,, $$
the inequalities (\ref{CylEnerPf_e1})-(\ref{CylEnerPf_e5}) give
$$ \big(1\!-\!4C^2\delta^2\big)\!\!\int_{[-t,t]\times S^1}\!\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2
\le \frac{2}{3}\big(1\!+\!4C^2\delta^2\big) 
\bigg(\int_{\{t\}\times S^1}|\textnormal{d} u|^2\textnormal{d}\theta
+\int_{\{-t\}\times S^1}|\textnormal{d} u|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\bigg).$$
Thus, the function 
$$\varepsilon(T)\equiv E_g\big(u;[-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]\big)
\equiv \frac12\int_{[-R+T,R-T]\times S^1}\!|\textnormal{d} u|^2\textnormal{d}\theta\textnormal{d} t$$
satisfies $\varepsilon(T)\!\le\!-\varepsilon'(T)$ for all $T\!\in\![-R,R]$,
if $\delta$ is sufficiently small (depending on~$C$).
This implies~(\ref{CylEner_e}).\\

\noindent
Let $h_{J,g}(x)\!=\!(x,\delta_{J,g}(x))$,
with $h_{J,g}(\cdot,\cdot)$ as in Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp}
and $\delta_{J,g}(\cdot)$ as provided by the previous paragraph.
Suppose $u$ also satisfies the last condition in Proposition~\ref{CylEner_prp}.
By Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp} and~(\ref{CylEner_e}),
$$|\textnormal{d}_{(t,\theta)}u|\le 3\sqrt{E_g(u;[-|t|\!-\!1,|t|\!+\!1]\!\times\!S^1)}
\le 3\sqrt{C_{J,g}(u(0,1))}\textnormal{e}^{(1+|t|-R)/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)}$$
for all $t\in[-R\!+\!1,R\!-\!1]$ and $\theta\!\in\!S^1$.
Thus, for all $t_1,t_2\!\in\![-R\!+\!T,R\!-\!T]$ with $T\!\ge\!1$ and 
$\theta_1,\theta_2\!\in\!S^1$,
\begin{equation*}\begin{split}
d_g\big(u(t_1,\theta_1),u(t_2,\theta_2)\big)
&\le 3\sqrt{C_{J,g}(u(0,1))E_g(u)}
\bigg(\pi\textnormal{e}^{(1+|t_1|-R)/2}+\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\!\textnormal{e}^{(1+|t|-R)/2}\textnormal{d} t\bigg)\\
&\le \big(3\pi\!+\!12\big) \sqrt{C_{J,g}(u(0,1))}\,\textnormal{e}^{(1-T)/2}\sqrt{E_g(u)}\,.
\end{split}\end{equation*}
This establishes~(\ref{CylEner_e2}).

and \hbox{$u_i\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$} is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps converging
uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$

\BE{fmdfn_e}\mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})\end{equation}

\end{enumerate}

\label{EnerPres3_lmm}
If $(X,J)$ is a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$,
then there exists a function $N\!:\mathbb R\!\longrightarrow\!{\mathbb Z}$ with the following property.
If $(\Sigma,\mathfrak j)$ is compact Riemann surface, $S_0\!\subset\!\Sigma$ is a finite subset,
 and $u_i\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps 
from open subsets of~$\Sigma$ with 
\BE{EnerPres3_e}U_i\subset U_{i+1}, \qquad \Sigma\!-\!S_0=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}\!U_i,
\quad\hbox{and}\quad E\!\equiv\!\liminf_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)<\infty,\end{equation}
then there exist a subset $S\!\subset\!\Sigma$ with $|S|\!\le\!N(E)\!+\!|S_0|$ 
and a subsequence of $u_i$ converging  uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology 
on compact subsets of $\Sigma\!-\!S$
to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$.

Let $\hbar_{J,g}$ be the minimal value of the function provided by Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp}.
For $E\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$, let $N(E)\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^{\ge0}$ be the smallest integer
such that $E\!\le\!N(E)\hbar_{J,g}$.\\

\noindent
Let $\Sigma$, $S_0$, $u_i$, and $E$ be as in the statement of the lemma and
$N\!=\!N(E)\!+\!|S_0|$.
Fix a Riemannian metric~$g_{\Sigma}$ on~$\Sigma$.
For $z\!\in\!\Sigma$ and $\delta\!\in\!\Sigma$, 
let $B_{\delta}(z)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ denote the ball of radius~$\delta$  around~$z$.
By Proposition~\ref{PtBnd_prp}, there exists $C\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ with the following property.
If $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a $J$-holomorphic map, $z\!\in\!\Sigma$, and $\delta\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$,
then
\BE{EnerPres3_e3}  E_g\big(u;B_{\delta}(z)\big)<\hbar_{J,g} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\big|\textnormal{d}_zu\big|_g\le C/\delta^2\,.\end{equation} 

\vspace{.1in}

\noindent
For every pair $i,j\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, 
let $\{z_{ij}^k\}_{k=1}^N$ be a subset of points of~$\Sigma$ containing~$S_0$ 
such~that
\BE{EnerPres3_e5} z\in \Sigma_{ij}^*\equiv\Sigma\!-\!\bigcup_{k=1}^N\!B_{2/j}\big(z_{ij}^k\big)
 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
E_g\big(u_i;B_{1/j}(z)\!\cap\!U_i\big)<\hbar_{J,g}\,.\end{equation}
By~(\ref{EnerPres3_e3}) and~(\ref{EnerPres3_e5}),
\BE{EnerPres3_e7} 
\big|\textnormal{d}_zu_i\big|_g\le Cj^2 \qquad\forall\,z\!\in\!\Sigma_{ij}^*
~\hbox{s.t.}~B_{1/j}(z)\!\subset\!U_i\,.\end{equation}

\vspace{.1in}

\noindent
After passing to a subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, we can assume that 
the sequence $E_g(u_i)$ converges to~$E$ and
that the sequence 
$\{z_{ij}^k\}_{i\in{\mathbb Z}^+}$ converges to some $z_j^k\!\in\!\Sigma$ for every 
$k\!=\!1,\ldots,N$ and $j\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$.
Along with~(\ref{EnerPres3_e7}) and 
the first two assumptions in~(\ref{EnerPres3_e}), this implies that 
\BE{EnerPres3_e9} \limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\big|\textnormal{d}_zu_i\big|_g\le Cj^2 
\qquad\forall\,z\in\Sigma_{ij}^*\,.\end{equation}
After passing to another subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, we can assume that the sequence 
$\{z_j^k\}_{j\in{\mathbb Z}^+}$ converges to some $z^k\!\in\!\Sigma$ for every 
$k\!=\!1,\ldots,N$.




\\

\noindent
By~(\ref{EnerPres3_e9}) and the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator, 
a subsequence of~$u_i$ converges  uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma_1^*$
to a $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$v_1\!:\Sigma_1^*\!\longrightarrow\!X$}.
By~(\ref{EnerPres3_e9}) and the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator,
a subsequence of this subsequence in turn converges  uniformly 
in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma_2^*$
to a $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$v_2\!:\Sigma_2^*\!\longrightarrow\!X$}.
Continuing in this way,  we obtain a subsequence of~$u_i$ 
converging  uniformly  in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma_j^*$
to a $J$-holomorphic map \hbox{$v_j\!:\Sigma_j^*\!\longrightarrow\!X$} for every $j\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$.
The limiting maps satisfy
$$v_j|_{\Sigma_j\cap\Sigma_{j'}^*}=v_{j'}|_{\Sigma_j^*\cap\Sigma_{j'}^*}
\qquad\forall~j,j'\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+\,.$$ 
Thus, the~map
$$u\!:\Sigma^*\!\equiv\!\Sigma^*\!-\!\big\{z^k\big\}\longrightarrow X, \qquad
u(z)=v_j(z)~~\forall\,z\!\in\!\Sigma_j^*,
$$
is well-defined and $J$-holomorphic.\\

\noindent
By construction, the final subsequence of $u_i$ converges  uniformly 
in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$\Sigma^*$ to~$u$.
This implies~that
$$E_g(u)\le \liminf_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)=E\,.$$
By Proposition~\ref{RemSing_prp}, $u$ thus extends to a $J$-holomorphic map $\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$.

\label{EnerPres_prp}
Let $(X,J)$ be a compact almost complex manifold with a Riemannian metric~$g$
and $u_i\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ be a sequence of $J$-holomorphic maps converging
uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$
to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:B_1\!\longrightarrow\!X$. If the limit
\BE{fmdfn_e2}\mathfrak m\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i;B_{\delta})\end{equation}

exists and is nonzero, then there exist
\begin{enumerate}[ref=\arabic*,label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=*]

\item a nodal Riemann surface $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ consisting of $B_1$ with 
a tree of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ attached at $0\!\in\!B_1$,

\item a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$,
 
\item a subsequence of $\{u_i\}$ still denoted by $\{u_i\}$, and

\item\label{psi_it} a biholomorphic map $\psi_i\!:U_i\!\longrightarrow\!B_{1/2}$, 
where $U_i\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ is an open subset,  

\end{enumerate}
such that 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\ref{psi_it}\alph*),leftmargin=*]

\item\label{Ccov_it} $E_g(u_{\infty};\Sigma_{\infty}\!-\!B_1)=\mathfrak m$, 
$U_i\!\subset\!U_{i+1}$, and $\mathbb{C}=\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty}U_i$,

\item\label{vcon_it} $u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i$ converges to~$u_{\infty}$ uniformly 
in the $C^{\infty}$-topology  on compact subsets of the complement of the nodes 
$\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_k^*$  in the sphere~$\mathbb{P}_0^1$ attached at $0\!\in\!B_1$,

\item\label{stab_it}  if $u_{\infty}|_{\mathbb{P}^1_0}$ is constant, 
$\mathbb{P}^1_0$ contains at least three nodes of~$\Sigma_{\infty}$;

\item (\ref{psi_it}) applies with $B_1$, $(\{u_i\},0)$,  and~$\mathfrak m$
replaced by  a neighborhood of~$w_r^*$ in~$\mathbb{C}$, $(\{u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i\},w_r^*)$, and 
\BE{fmdfn_e3}\mathfrak m_r'\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}
E_g\big(u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i;B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big),\end{equation}
respectively, for each $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$.

\end{enumerate}

Let $\hbar_{J,g}$ be the smaller of the numbers $\hbar_{J,g}$
in Corollaries~\ref{LowEner_crl} and~\ref{EnerPres2_crl}.
In particular, $\mathfrak m\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$.\\



 






\noindent
For each $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large, choose $z_i\!\in\!\ov{B_{1/2}}$ so~that
\BE{maxdui_e} \max_{z\in \ov{B_{1/2}}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|_g=\big|\textnormal{d}_{z_i}u_i\big|_g.\end{equation}
Since $u_i$ converges
uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology on compact subsets of~$B_1^*$ to~$u$,
$z_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$.
Thus,  $B_{1/2}(z_i)\!\subset\!B_1$
for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large.
By Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm}\ref{dela_it},
for all $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large there exists $\delta_i\!\in\!(0,1/2)$
such~that 
\BE{dejidfn_e} E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i)\big)=\mathfrak m-\frac{\hbar_{J,g}}{2}\,.\end{equation}
Define
$$\psi_i\!:U_i\!\equiv\!\big\{w\!\in\!\mathbb{C}\!: z_i\!+\!\delta_iw\!\in\!B_{1/2}\big\}
\longrightarrow B_{1/2}
\qquad\hbox{by}\qquad \psi_i(w)=z_i\!+\!\delta_iw\,.$$
Since $\delta_i\!\longrightarrow\!0$, the second property in \ref{Ccov_it} holds.\\

\noindent
For each $i\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$ sufficiently large, let
$$v_i=u_i\!\circ\!\psi_i\!:  U_i\longrightarrow X.$$
Since $u_i$ is $J$-holomorphic and $\psi_i$ is biholomorphic onto its image,
$v_i$ is a $J$-holomorphic map with \hbox{$E_g(v_i)=E_g(u_i;B_{1/2})$}.
Along with Lemma~\ref{EnerPres1_lmm}\ref{SeqEner_it}, this implies that
$$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(v_i)=\mathfrak m(1/2)<\infty\,.$$
By Lemma~\ref{EnerPres3_lmm}, there thus exist a finite collection 
$w_1^*,\ldots,w_k^*\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ of distinct points 
and a subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, still denoted by~$\{u_i\}$, 
such that $v_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology
on compact subsets  of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_{\ell}^*\}$
to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$.
In particular, \ref{vcon_it} holds and
$|\textnormal{d} v_i|_g$ is uniformly bounded on compact subsets 
of $\mathbb{P}^1\!-\!\{\infty,w_1^*,\ldots,w_{\ell}^*\}$.
We can also assume that the limit~(\ref{fmdfn_e3})
exists for every $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$.
We note~that
\BE{EnerBub_e}\begin{split}
E_g(v)+\!\sum_{r=1}^k\!\mathfrak m_r' 
&=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!
E_g\!\big(v_i,B_R\!-\!\bigcup_{r=1}^k\! B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big)
+\sum_{r=1}^k\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g\big(v_i;B_{\delta}(w_r^*)\big)\\
&=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g\big(v_i,B_R\big)
=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\!\!E_g\big(u_i,B_{R\delta_i}(z_i)\big)=\mathfrak m\,;
\end{split}\end{equation}
the last equality holds by~(\ref{noEloss_e1}).\\


\noindent
Let $\delta_0\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be such that the balls $B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)$ are pairwise disjoint.
If 
$$\limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\max_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} v_i\big|<\infty$$
for some~$r$, then $\{v_i\}$ converges  uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology
on $\ov{B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)}$ to~$v$ by the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator.
Thus, we can assume~that 
$$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\sup_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} v_i\big|=\infty$$
for every $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$.
In light of  Corollary~\ref{EnerPres2_crl}\ref{fmLowBnd_it}, $\mathfrak m_r'\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$.\\

\noindent
We next show that $u(0)\!=\!v(\infty)$, i.e.~that the bubble $(\mathbb{P}_0^1,v)$ 
connects to $(B_1,u)$ at~$z\!=\!0$.
Note~that
\begin{equation*}\begin{split}
d_g\big(u(0),v(\infty)\big)
&=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}d_g\big(u(\delta),v(R)\big)
=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}d_g\big(u_i(z_i\!+\!\delta),v_i(R)\big)\\
&=\lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}
d_g\big(u_i(z_i\!+\!\delta),u_i(z_i\!+\!R\delta_i)\big)\\
&\le \lim_{R\longrightarrow\infty}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}
\textnormal{diam}_g\big(u_i(B_{\delta}(z_i)\!-\!B_{R\delta_i}(z_i))\big).
\end{split}\end{equation*}
Along with~(\ref{noEloss_e2}), this implies that $u(0)\!=\!v(\infty)$.\\

\noindent
Suppose $v\!:\mathbb{P}^1\!\longrightarrow\!X$ is a constant map.
By~(\ref{EnerBub_e}), $k\!\ge\!1$ and so there exists $w^*\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ such that 
$|\textnormal{d}_{w^*}v_i|\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$.
By~(\ref{maxdui_e}) and the definition of~$\psi_i$, 
$|\textnormal{d}_0v_i|\!\ge\!|\textnormal{d}_wv_i|$ for all $w\!\in\!\mathbb{C}$ contained in the domain of~$v_i$
and so $|\textnormal{d}_0v_i|\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$ as $i\!\longrightarrow\!\infty$.
By~(\ref{fmdfn_e3}) and~(\ref{dejidfn_e}), 
$$\mathfrak m_0'\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}
E_g(v_i)
\le \lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g\big(v_i;B_1\big)
=\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty} E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta_i}(z_i)\big)
= \mathfrak m-\frac{\hbar}{2}<\mathfrak m,$$
and so $k\!\ge\!2$, as claimed in~\ref{stab_it}.
Since the amount of energy of $v_i$ contained in $\mathbb{C}\!-\!B_1$ approaches $\hbar_{J,g}/2$,
as illustrated in Figure~\ref{EnerDist_fig},
there must be in particular a bubble point~$w_r^*$ with $|w_r^*|\!=\!1$,
though this is not material.\\

\noindent
The above establishes Proposition~\ref{EnerPres_prp} whenever $k\!=\!0$ by
taking 
$$u_{\infty}\big|_{B^1}=u \qquad\hbox{and}\qquad u_{\infty}\big|_{\mathbb{P}^1_0}=v.$$
Since $\mathfrak m_r'\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$ for every~$r$, $k\!=\!0$ if $\mathfrak m\!<\!2\hbar_{J,g}$.
If $k\!\ge\!1$, $\mathfrak m_r'\!\le\!\mathfrak m\!-\!\hbar_{J,g}$ by~(\ref{EnerBub_e})
because 
\hbox{$E_g(v)\!\ge\!\hbar_{J,g}$} if $v$ is not constant by Corollary~\ref{LowEner_crl}
and $k\!\ge\!2$ otherwise by the above.
Thus, by induction on $[\mathfrak m/\hbar_{J,g}]\!\in\!{\mathbb Z}^+$, we can assume that 
Proposition~\ref{EnerPres_prp} holds when applied to~$\{v_i\}$ on 
$B_{\delta_0}(w_r^*)\!\subset\!\mathbb{C}$ with $r\!=\!1,\ldots,k$.
This yields a tree~$\Sigma_r$ of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ with a distinguished smooth point~$\infty$
and a $J$-holomorphic map $v_r\!:\Sigma_r\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such $v_r(\infty)\!=\!v(w_r^*)$ and
$E_g(v_r)\!=\!\mathfrak m_r'$.
Combining the last equality with~(\ref{EnerBub_e}), we obtain
$$E_g(v)+\!\sum_{r=1}^k\!E_g(v_r)=\mathfrak m\,.$$
Identifying $\infty$ in the base sphere of each~$\Sigma_r$ with $w_r^*\!\in\!\mathbb{P}_0^1$,
which has been already attached to $0\!\in\!B_1^*$, we obtain
a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$ with the desired properties;
see Figure~\ref{GrLim_fig2}.

Fix a Riemannian metric~$g_{\Sigma}$ on~$\Sigma$.
For $z\!\in\!\Sigma$ and $\delta\!\in\!\Sigma$, 
let $B_{\delta}(z)\!\subset\!\Sigma$ denote the ball of radius~$\delta$  around~$z$.\\

\noindent
By Lemma~\ref{EnerPres3_lmm}, there exist a finite collection 
$z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\!\in\!\Sigma$ of distinct points 
and a subsequence of~$\{u_i\}$, still denoted by~$\{u_i\}$, 
such that $u_i$ converges uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology
on compact subsets  of $\Sigma\!-\!\{z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\}$
to a $J$-holomorphic map $u\!:\Sigma\!\longrightarrow\!X$.
In particular, $|\textnormal{d} u_i|_g$ is uniformly bounded on compact subsets 
of $\Sigma\!-\!\{z_1^*,\ldots,z_{\ell}^*\}$.
We can also assume that  the~limit
$$\mathfrak m_j\equiv\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_j^*)\big)$$
exists for every $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$.
We note that 
\BE{Egtot_e}\begin{split} 
E_g(u)+\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\mathfrak m_j&=
\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u;\Sigma\!-\!\bigcup_{j=1}^{\ell}B_{\delta}(z_j^*)\big)
+\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g\big(u_i;B_{\delta}(z_j^*)\big)\\
&=\lim_{\delta\longrightarrow0}\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)=\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i).\\
\end{split}\end{equation}

\vspace{.1in}

\noindent
Let $\delta_0\!\in\!\mathbb R^+$ be such that the balls $B_{\delta_0}(z_i^*)$ are pairwise disjoint.
If 
$$\limsup_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\max_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_j^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|<\infty$$
for some~$j$, then $\{u_i\}$ converges  uniformly in the $C^{\infty}$-topology
on $\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_j^*)}$ to~$u$ by the ellipticity of the $\bar\partial$-operator.
Thus, we can assume~that 
$$\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}\sup_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_i^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|=\infty$$
for every $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$.\\


\noindent
For each $j\!=\!1,\ldots,\ell$, Proposition~\ref{EnerPres_prp} provides
a tree~$\Sigma_j$ of Riemann spheres~$\mathbb{P}^1$ with a distinguished smooth point~$\infty$
and a $J$-holomorphic map $v_j\!:\Sigma_j\!\longrightarrow\!X$ such $v_j(\infty)\!=\!v(w_r^*)$ and
$E_g(v_j)\!=\!\mathfrak m_j$.
Combining the last equality with~(\ref{Egtot_e}), we obtain
$$E_g(v)+\!\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\!E_g(v_j)=\lim_{i\longrightarrow\infty}E_g(u_i)\,.$$
Identifying the distinguished point~$\infty$ of each~$\Sigma_j$ with $z_j^*\!\in\!\Sigma$,
we obtain a Riemann surface $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty})$ and 
a $J$-holomorphic map $u_{\infty}\!:\Sigma_{\infty}\!\longrightarrow\!X$ with the desired properties.\\

\noindent
If $\Sigma\!=\!\mathbb{P}^1$ and the limit map~$u$ above is constant,
then $\ell\!\ge\!1$ by~(\ref{Egtot_e}).
Suppose $\ell\!\in\!\{1,2\}$. 
Let
$$M_i=\sup_{\ov{B_{\delta_0}(z_1^*)}}\big|\textnormal{d} u_i\big|$$
and parametrize~$\mathbb{P}^1$ so that $z_1^*\!=\!0$.
Define 
$$h_i\!: \mathbb{P}^1\longrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1, \qquad  h_i(z)=z_i\!+\!z/M_i,$$
and apply the preceding argument with $u_i$ replaced by~$u_i\!\circ\!h_i$.
By the proof of Corollary~\ref{EnerPres2_crl}\ref{fmLowBnd_it}, the limiting map $u|_{\Sigma}$
is then non-constant and $(\Sigma_{\infty},\mathfrak j_{\infty},u)$ is a stable $J$-holomorphic map.
